source.basis: Operator facility page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
EdgeCore Ashburn AS02 publishes 114 MW of IT capacity, third among Virginia data centers that disclose a figure and 7.1 percent of the state's published total.

The pattern here is disclosure scarcity, not capacity scarcity. Virginia has 330 mapped data centers, but only 25 publish megawatt figures, and those 25 sum to 1,603 MW. One campus holding 7.1 percent of that disclosed load shows how few facilities the published total actually rests on. The real state figure is larger, by an amount the data does not quantify.

For AI, 114 MW is the operative number. That is enough IT load to run accelerator-dense training or serving at scale, and it sits in Ashburn, inside Northern Virginia's existing power and network backbone. The 685,000 square feet of technical space and the LEED certification describe the building and its operations, not the compute installed inside it.

What this does not cover is as important as what it does. Grid constraints on further expansion in Virginia are not published here. Neither are actual utilization, whether the 114 MW is leased or committed, or the capacity of the roughly 305 mapped facilities that publish nothing. The figure is operator-published, not independently measured.
